definitions.gloss: hypothetical form; the conditional conjugation form of Japanese verbs and adjectives, used with ～ば to express 'if'
definitions.explanation: hypothetical form; the conditional conjugation form of Japanese verbs and adjectives, used with ～ば to express 'if'

examples.japanese: {仮定形|かていけい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{作|つく}り{方|かた}→作り方：27938_tsukurikata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}しましょう→練習する：22991_renshuusuru⟧。
examples.english: Let's practice how to form the hypothetical form.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{動詞|どうし}→動詞：03472_doushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{六|ろく}→六：00747_roku⟧つ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{活用形|かつようけい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あり→ある：00006_aru⟧、{仮定形|かていけい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦そのうち→そのうち：00380_sonouchi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Japanese verbs have six conjugation forms, and the hypothetical form is one of them.

notes:
A grammatical term used in Japanese language education. In the traditional six-form conjugation system (⟦{活用|かつよう}→活用：02620_katsuyou⟧), the {仮定形|かていけい} is the form that attaches to the conditional particle ば. For godan verbs, this is the え-row form (e.g., ⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧ → ⟦{書|か}けば→書く：00477_kaku⟧); for ichidan verbs, it ends in れば (e.g., ⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ → ⟦{食|た}べれば→食べる：00396_taberu⟧).

THE SIX CONJUGATION FORMS:
- ⟦{未然形|みぜんけい}→未然形：23610_mizenkei⟧ — irrealis form (connects to ⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧, よう, etc.)
- ⟦{連用形|れんようけい}→連用形：16646_renyoukei⟧ — continuative form (connects to ます, た, etc.)
- ⟦{終止形|しゅうしけい}→終止形：23611_shuushikei⟧ — terminal form (dictionary form)
- ⟦{連体形|れんたいけい}→連体形：23612_rentaikei⟧ — attributive form (before nouns)
- {仮定形|かていけい} — hypothetical form (connects to ば)
- ⟦{命令形|めいれいけい}→命令形：22948_meireikei⟧ — imperative form

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {条件形|じょうけんけい} — conditional form (an alternative name sometimes used in textbooks)
- ⟦{已然形|いぜんけい}→已然形：26736_izenkei⟧ — realis form (the classical Japanese predecessor of the {仮定形|かていけい})
